subject: Re: Dependency mapping and region safeguard request
messages:
From: Alan Miller <alan.miller@northshorebank.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northshorebank.com, securityteam@northshorebank.com
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Dependency map + region safeguard question

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our vendor diligence for the upcoming core ledger integration, the security team needs a short dependency map that lists (1) every third-party operator or infra partner that may process tokenized customer data, (2) the regions where those operators are permitted to operate for our account, and (3) any planned region deprecations or provider swaps in the next 12 months that could affect failover.

Specifically: can you confirm whether any of your cloud or operator partners are scheduled to decommission EU-west-3 or shift workloads out of the London region in the next year? We need this to sign off on our data residency controls.

If possible, please attach a CSV roster and a short narrative describing fallback assurances. We can treat the roster as confidential.

Appreciate it — Alan
Alan Miller
Senior Manager, Vendor Risk
NorthShore Bank

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alan Miller <alan.miller@northshorebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 11:04:16 -0800
Subject: Re: Dependency map + region safeguard question

Alan — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching the vendor roster CSV and a region map PDF. High level answers up front:

- No scheduled decommission of eu-west-3 (London) that would affect customer workloads for the next 12 months under current plans.
- We maintain explicit region allowlists per customer; for NorthShore we're not routing any production traffic through experimental EU regions.
- If an operator change were required for capacity or compliance, we have a documented fallback playbook and a 30-day notice cadence; see attached "safeguard_playbook_v1.docx".

Quick notes about the attachments: vendor_roster lists our subprocessor role for each provider plus contact and region allowances. The region_map shows primary/secondary locations and cross-region SLA tiers.

Next steps: Kimberly is copied and can add technical details on how we isolate KV-caches and control routing. If you want a redacted version for broader distribution I can prepare that.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_vendor_roster_2027-11.csv (CSV, 42KB); cloud_provider_region_map_2027.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alan Miller <alan.miller@northshorebank.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 12:18:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Dependency map + region safeguard question

Alan — adding a quick technical supplement here.

- For the NorthShore Dedicated environment we pin control-plane routing to a set of certified operators (listed in the CSV). Runtime inference is served from pinned model deployment groups; we never do automatic cross-region failover without an explicit customer policy.
- KV cache and prefix caching are scoped per-tenant; we encrypt caches with customer-specific keys (KMS). That prevents spillover if an operator changes regions.
- Planned provider updates: one of our partner edge operators (NebulaEdge) is evaluating footprint changes in Q2 2028; however, NebulaEdge is not in the list of operators permitted for NorthShore production workloads. Any change there would be limited to non-production edge routing.

If you want, I can produce a short matrix mapping each subprocessor to the exact GCP/AWS/Azure regions they are authorized to use for NorthShore.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Cloud Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications: (1) can you explicitly confirm NebulaEdge is excluded from NorthShore production routing as of today? (2) procurement wants an affirmative note on whether Redwood will provide 30-day notice for subprocessor region changes and whether that notice will include a migration plan with rollback steps.

Also copying Sara Lopez from our external risk advisor (s.lopez@vendorrisk.com) who will review the roster.

Regards,
Alan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alan Miller <alan.miller@northshorebank.com>, procurement@northshorebank.com, Sara Lopez <s.lopez@vendorrisk.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 15:43:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Dependency map + region safeguard question

Alan/Sara/Procurement — answering both bullets formally for your audit record: 

1) NebulaEdge: confirmed excluded. NebulaEdge is part of our brokered edge ecosystem but is NOT authorized for NorthShore production workloads. We have an allowlist enforced in the control plane; NebulaEdge appears in the roster only as a potential partner for non-prod edge testing.

2) 30-day notice and migration plan: Redwood commits to a 30 calendar day notification for any change that affects a customer-authorized region or subprocessor list. That notice will include:
   - The effective change date and impacted services
   - A migration plan with expected downtime windows (if any) and rollback steps
   - Contact information for the operator and Redwood escalation path
   - A point-by-point QA checklist we use to validate successful migration (we can share a template)

We've attached a one-page extract from our internal playbook summarizing the notification mechanics and our SLAs. For procurement: we are happy to put this into the contract SOW and to accept a notification milestone that aligns with your internal change control.

Attachments: safeguard_playbook_v1.docx (DOCX, 85KB)

If you'd like, we can schedule a short 30-minute call to walk procurement and security through the playbook and the roster.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0191
